title: A family isomorphic to a covering is a covering
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site in the sense of Stacks Sites, Definition 00VH [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1): a category with a set $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ of families of morphisms with fixed target such that (i) $\{V\to U\}$ is a covering for every isomorphism $V\to U$, (ii) if $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering and $\{V_{ij}\to U_i\}_{j\in J_i}$ is a covering for every $i$ then $\{V_{ij}\to U\}_{i,j}$ is a covering, (iii) for a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and a morphism $V\to U$ the fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ exist and, for some choice of them, $\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering. Let $\{g_a:U_a\to U\}_{a\in A}$ be a covering of $\mathcal C$, and let $\{f_a:V_a\to V\}_{a\in A}$ be a family of morphisms of $\mathcal C$ with common target, indexed by the same set $A$, together with an isomorphism $\varphi:V\to U$ and isomorphisms $\sigma_a:V_a\to U_a$ such that $g_a\circ\sigma_a=\varphi\circ f_a$ for every $a\in A$. Then $\{f_a:V_a\to V\}_{a\in A}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$. (In particular, for $\varphi=\mathrm{id}$: replacing the sources of a covering by isomorphic objects over the target gives a covering.)
